items.title: Keeping the patient's words: design of Aperta Health, a clinician-governed AI documentation-support prototype for multilingual and refugee mental health care in Australia
items.abstract: In the 2021 Census, 5.8 million people in Australia (22.8%) used a language other than English at home, and 872,000 said they spoke English not well or not at all. For people from refugee and migrant backgrounds, the first barrier to mental health care is often simply being understood. Services report that many clinicians do not engage interpreters, and when a consultation does cross languages, the patient's own words, idioms and explanations of distress are easily lost between the interpreter, the clinician and the record. Victoria's Royal Commission into its mental health system recommended developing digital technologies to deliver language services. This paper reports the design of Aperta Health, a web-based prototype that uses generative AI to help clinicians and bicultural workers turn multilingual or interpreter-mediated accounts into a structured, safety-conscious clinical record without discarding the original words. Its core design move is a strict division of labour. Deterministic code scores screening instruments and applies coded crisis rules. Generative AI only extracts, translates and drafts within bounded formats, and is told to write "Not stated in narrative" rather than invent findings. Qualified professionals interpret, diagnose, prescribe and escalate. We describe the design principles and architecture, then assess the prototype against Australian regulation. We conclude that several functions, including AI-drafted diagnostic formulations and public self-assessment, would be unlikely to qualify for the Therapeutic Goods Administration's exemption for clinical decision support software, and that the prototype's data flows do not yet meet the privacy expectations set out in national clinical AI guidance. We state these limits plainly. The prototype runs only on synthetic data, has not been clinically evaluated, and is not supplied for clinical use. The contribution is a reusable design pattern for language-inclusive mental health documentation, and an honest map of what stands between such a prototype and safe use. items.title: Key Data Analytics Trends to Explore Before Choosing a Data Analytics
items.abstract: Data analytics is changing how organisations operate, plan, and compete. Businesses use data to understand customer behaviour, improve services, reduce costs, and identify new opportunities. As digital systems expand, companies collect information from websites, applications, transactions, supply chains, and customer interactions. They need skilled professionals who can turn this information into clear and useful insights. At the same time, the field is evolving. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, cloud analytics, real-time reporting, and automated data preparation are changing how analysts work. These developments are creating new opportunities, but they also require learners to build strong foundations and keep their skills current. Choosing a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet requires more than checking a course title. Learners should understand the current trends in the industry, the tools employers use, and the skills required for different career paths. This knowledge can help them select relevant training and prepare for the changing demands of the data analytics profession. The Growing Importance of Data Analytics Organisations no longer use data only to prepare monthly reports. They use it to support decisions across sales, finance, marketing, operations, healthcare, manufacturing, and technology. For example, a retailer can analyse sales records to forecast product demand. A bank can study transaction patterns to identify suspicious activity. A hospital can use operational reports to plan staff and resources. A marketing team can measure campaign performance to understand which activities produce results. These applications depend on accurate data, suitable analytical methods, and clear communication. Analysts must understand the business problem before selecting tools or drawing conclusions. The market outlook also reflects the growing role of analytics. Grand View Research estimated that India's data analytics market generated approximately US$4.23 billion in revenue in 2025 and projected that it could reach around US$47.51 billion by 2033. The forecast represents an estimated compound annual growth rate of 36.1% from 2026 to 2033. These are market projections, not guaranteed employment or salary outcomes. For learners considering a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet, this growth highlights the value of developing practical skills that can be applied across industries. Artificial Intelligence and AI-Assisted Analytics Artificial intelligence is one of the most important trends in the analytics industry. AI tools can help analysts summarise datasets, identify patterns, generate queries, and automate routine tasks. This can reduce the time spent on some activities and allow professionals to focus more on interpreting results. For example, an analyst can use AI-assisted tools to explore sales performance or generate an initial summary of customer feedback. The analyst must still verify the output, check the data, and confirm that the conclusions are valid. In June 2026, Gartner identified AI-first operations, AI governance, and connected data and analytics platforms among the major trends shaping enterprise analytics. Its report also highlighted the need to manage the risks associated with AI-driven decisions. Learners should therefore understand both the benefits and the limits of AI. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet can provide a foundation in data analysis, while further learning can help students explore AI-assisted workflows. Important areas to understand include: Using AI tools to support data exploration. Checking AI-generated calculations and summaries. Understanding the basics of machine learning. Protecting confidential information when using AI systems. Applying human judgement to important business decisions. AI can support analytical work, but it does not remove the need for accurate data, sound reasoning, and accountability. Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics Traditional reporting often explains what has already happened. Predictive and prescriptive analytics extend this process by helping organisations estimate possible outcomes and assess potential actions. Predictive Analytics Predictive analytics uses historical data, statistical methods, and machine learning models to estimate future events. A retailer may forecast product demand from previous sales. A financial institution may estimate credit risk. A logistics company may use historical delivery information to identify the factors linked to delays. Learners should understand basic statistics, data preparation, and model evaluation before moving into advanced predictive techniques. Python and SQL can also support this work. Prescriptive Analytics Prescriptive analytics goes a step further by assessing possible actions based on defined objectives and constraints. For example, a supply chain team may use an optimisation model to assess delivery routes or inventory levels. Grand View Research identified predictive analytics as the largest segment of India's data analytics market by revenue in 2025, while its forecast identified prescriptive analytics as the fastest-growing type segment over the projection period. These developments show the value of understanding analytical methods beyond basic reporting. Learners considering a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should review whether the syllabus covers statistical reasoning and introduces advanced analytics at an appropriate level. Real-Time Data Analytics and Streaming Businesses increasingly need information as events occur. Real-time analytics helps teams monitor new data and respond to changes without waiting for a monthly or weekly report. For example, an e-commerce company can track order activity and inventory levels during a major sale. A transport company can monitor vehicle performance and delivery status. A financial organisation can use real-time systems to flag transactions that require further review. Real-time analytics often depends on data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, streaming technologies, and reliable monitoring systems. Entry-level analysts may not build these systems themselves, but an understanding of how data moves from source to dashboard can help them work more effectively with technical teams. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should ideally teach learners the fundamentals of data collection, cleaning, and reporting before introducing more advanced real-time applications. Cloud Analytics and Modern Data Platforms Cloud analytics allows organisations to store, process, and analyse data through cloud-based services. It can help teams access information across locations and connect datasets from different business systems. Cloud platforms also support collaboration and scalable data processing. However, effective cloud analytics requires suitable access controls, cost management, data quality checks, and security practices. Modern data platforms increasingly bring together data engineering, analytics, governance, and AI capabilities. This creates a need for professionals who understand not only how to create a report but also where the data comes from and how it should be used. For beginners, the practical starting point is to understand spreadsheets, databases, SQL, data models, and visualisation tools. After building this foundation, learners can explore cloud data services and more advanced analytical workflows. Business Intelligence and Data Visualisation Business intelligence remains a key part of modern analytics. Organisations need clear dashboards and reports that help teams monitor performance and act on relevant findings. Tools such as Microsoft Power BI and Tableau help users present information through charts, tables, filters, and interactive dashboards. Excel remains useful for organising data and performing basic analysis. A well-designed dashboard can show revenue trends, customer retention, inventory levels, and operating costs in one place. The analyst must choose suitable metrics and explain their meaning without creating misleading impressions. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet that includes practical reporting exercises can help learners understand these concepts. When reviewing a programme, check whether it covers data preparation, dashboard design, data modelling, and the interpretation of business metrics. Data Quality, Privacy, and Responsible Analytics Advanced tools cannot compensate for poor-quality data. Missing values, duplicate records, incorrect formats, and inconsistent definitions can lead to inaccurate reports. Data quality and governance have become even more important as organisations expand their use of AI and self-service analytics. TechTarget's January 2026 review of business intelligence trends highlighted governance, data quality, and responsible access to analytics as important concerns for organisations. Learners should develop habits that support reliable analysis: Check the source and completeness of a dataset. Identify duplicate records and inconsistent values. Confirm that calculations use the correct definitions. Protect personal and confidential information. Document assumptions and limitations. Avoid drawing conclusions that the data cannot support. These practices apply to every industry. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should help learners recognise that responsible data handling is part of professional analytics, not an optional extra. items.abstract: Abstract Radiological reports, which document radiologists’ imaging observations and diagnostic conclusions from CT, X-ray and MRI scans, deliver core imaging evidence for clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Inaccurate or disordered reports may lead to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention, posing risks to patient safety. Radiological reports are essential for clinical decision-making, yet Chinese radiology reports frequently exhibit logical inconsistencies, incomplete content, non-standardized descriptions, and formatting errors, while manual quality control remains time-consuming and inconsistent. Large teacher models can provide task-specific supervision but are difficult to deploy locally, whereas smaller models require adaptation to this clinical text task. We developed a teacher-supervised, locally deployable 4B language-model system for rule-based textual quality control of Chinese radiology reports.Among the three evaluated teacher APIs, Doubao-seed1.6-non-thinking achieved the highest macro-precision ,0.94, under the study's precision-prioritized selection.Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 emerged as the optimal student model, achieving an average precision of 0.90, recall of 0.49, and F1 score of 0.62, with inference speed improved by over 40-fold. Real-world clinical validation demonstrated that the lightweight model attains a precision of 0.74 in authentic clinical scenarios while retaining high overall performance, satisfying the deployment demands of on-site clinical institutions.

items.title: KVCompass: A Discovery Plane for Internet-Scale Prefix Cache Sharing in LLM Serving
items.abstract: KV cache reuse is one of the most effective ways to reduce LLM inference cost, but today its benefits are largely confined to a single cluster. When a provider serves the same model across geographically distributed regions, each region may repeatedly prefill the same popular prefixes, wasting GPU time and increasing time-to-first-token (TTFT). Exploiting reuse across regions involves discovering which worker currently holds a reusable KV cache for each request's prefix. We show that this KV cache discovery problem is structurally harder than conventional object lookup. Unlike hash-placement mechanisms such as DHTs, where an object's location is a deterministic function of its key, KV caches are created on the workers that serve requests, and their holder sets change with subsequent requests and KV cache evictions. KV cache discovery therefore calls for decoupling KV cache identity from placement. We present KVCompass, a discovery plane for Internet-scale KV cache sharing. The discovery index supports variable-length prefix lookup with constant-time local table reads at the edge, allowing each request to be forwarded to the worker that best balances KV cache reuse against load and network distance. Evaluation includes a 64-worker geo-distributed simulation and a 14-worker three-continent real-machine testbed. Evaluation shows that KVCompass achieves $1.3-14\times$ lower P99 TTFT than the baselines, up to $3.7\times$ lower P99 end-to-end latency, up to $4.7\times$ the throughput, and a peak load factor within 2% of the Oracle floor.

items.title: La articulación de un trinomio pedagógico: transversalidad, competencias y aprendizaje centrado en el estudiante.
items.abstract: This review article examines how three key variables of contemporary educational reform come together: curricular mainstreaming, competency-based learning, and student-centeredness. Drawing on a qualitative, descriptive and documentary methodology based on the systematization of twenty relevant studies published between 2024 and 2026, it analyzes the behavior, evolution and operational tensions among these pedagogical trends. The results show that mainstreaming works as the methodological scaffold that unsettles fragmented traditional knowledge and enables the mobilization of complex competencies in the classroom. They also confirm that student-centered approaches meaningfully increase intrinsic motivation, socio-environmental awareness and critical thinking skills. The study reviews operational limitations as well, including teacher resistance and the administrative complexity involved in designing integrated curricula. It concludes that the convergence of these three dimensions is not a decorative addition to didactic planning but a necessary condition for building a deep, ethical education with a strong sense of civic responsibility amid the dynamics of the knowledge society.

items.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.

items.title: Large Diffusion Models Need More Than EMA
items.abstract: Large-scale diffusion models are commonly trained with a constant learning rate (LR) and exponential moving average (EMA), despite the strong performance of LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization in training large language models. We study whether EMA is uniquely suited to diffusion training, or whether stronger alternatives have been underexplored. Our theory shows that averaging a constant-step trajectory has an inherent optimization limitation, whereas LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization admit vanishing stationarity guarantees under standard nonconvex assumptions. Empirically, LR decay and EMA provide complementary benefits: combining decay with EMA further improves the standard baseline at most tested starting points, although the gain remains sensitive to when decay begins. Schedule-Free avoids this timing requirement and consistently outperforms EMA with a constant LR across training stages, achieving both lower fixed-evaluation objectives and better generation quality. Our analysis further shows that all three strategies substantially reduce parameter variability, yet stronger stabilization is not always better: EMA with a constant LR retains comparatively higher parameter variability, while aggressive decay combined with EMA achieves the lowest checkpoint variability but also weakens continued optimization. Schedule-Free substantially reduces parameter variability while preserving more late-stage progress, providing a better balance between parameter stability and continued optimization. Finally, the benefits of Schedule-Free extend beyond pretraining to ReFL and generator-side DMD, demonstrating its transferability across distinct diffusion optimization settings. Overall, our results suggest that large diffusion models need more than parameter averaging alone: effective optimization requires balancing variance reduction with continued optimization.

items.title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists’ agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text. Results Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ : 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87–84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10–89.61%). Conclusion In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists’ agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows. Key Points Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231–0.775), narrowing the junior–senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91–81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

items.title: Laryngeal Findings And Laryngopharyngeal Reflux In Open-Air Market Vendors: A Cross-Sectional Videolaryngoscopic Study
items.abstract: Purpose: To describe laryngeal disorders among open-air market vendors and identify the most prevalent disorders, lesion types, affected laryngeal regions, and associated risk factors.Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted involving 49 open-air market vendors from Aracaju, Northeastern Brazil.Participants underwent structured interviews and videonasolaryngoscopic examination.Demographic, occupational, clinical, and laryngeal findings were analyzed descriptively.Results: Women represented 63.3% of participants.Hoarseness was reported by 55% of the sample.Symptoms suggestive of laryngopharyngeal reflux were highly prevalent.Videolaryngoscopy revealed abnormalities in all laryngeal compartments, with the highest prevalence occurring in the posterior laryngeal and subglottic regions.Interarytenoid and retrocricoid edema and hyperemia, with or without pachydermia, were the predominant findings.Vocal fold cysts predominated among women, whereas vocal fold thickening and polyps were more common among men.Conclusion: Open-air market vendors should be considered a distinct category of professional voice users.Laryngopharyngeal reflux was the most prevalent disorder and the posterior laryngeal/subglottic region was the most frequently affected site.Preventive occupational health measures focusing on vocal hygiene and reflux control are warranted.

items.title: Latent profiles of work readiness and their associated factors among nursing interns: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Work readiness refers to the comprehensive competencies required for individuals to enter and adapt to the workforce. It is relevant to the transition from nursing student to clinical nurse. However, existing research has paid limited attention to heterogeneity in nursing interns’ work readiness, and few studies have examined associated factors from the perspective of Social Cognitive Career Theory. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of work readiness among nursing interns and examine the associations of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) literacy and the clinical learning environment with profile membership. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 712 final-year nursing interns from three nursing schools in Anhui Province, China, between November 2025 and June 2026. Participants completed the Nursing Practice Readiness Scale, Clinical Learning Environment Questionnaire, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale. Latent Profile Analysis was used to identify distinct work readiness profiles, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with profile membership. Results Three latent profiles of work readiness were identified: low work readiness ( n = 415, 58.3%), moderate work readiness ( n = 227, 31.9%), and high work readiness ( n = 70, 9.8%). The overall multinomial logistic regression model( χ 2 = 467.253, P < 0.001) showed that the clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were significantly associated with work readiness profile membership (all P < 0.05). Conclusions Three distinct work readiness profiles were identified among nursing interns. Clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of nursing interns’ work readiness and may inform the development of individualized educational support strategies.

items.title: Leading the Future
items.abstract: Generative AI will shape health care less through model fluency alone than through the workforce and institutions prepared to use it responsibly. Anchored in UCLA Health’s randomized trial of ambient AI scribes, this chapter treats generative AI as workforce infrastructure: a socio-technical arrangement involving models, interfaces, consent, training, review, supervision, and local support. Evidence from ambient documentation, AI-assisted inbox replies, patient messaging, and UC Health’s developing memory-care redesign shows that generative AI does not eliminate professional responsibility; it redistributes work from first-draft production toward verification, exception handling, relational communication, supervision, and workflow redesign. Placed within the book’s five transformations, these tools can accelerate capture, synthesis, and drafting, but cannot replace standards, governance, or accountable enactment. The chapter identifies hallucination, omission, overconfidence, hidden correction burden, uneven adoption, privacy, and changing local conditions as limits requiring continuous stewardship. It then defines the next-generation workforce through integrated capabilities in AI and data literacy, critical appraisal, escalation judgment, human factors, patient communication, interdisciplinary collaboration, change management, and bioequity monitoring. Education must therefore move beyond prompting to supervised practice and accountable review. The chapter concludes that future readiness requires portfolio visibility, role-specific training, explicit review and escalation standards, patient transparency, postdeployment monitoring, redesign capacity, and leadership able to preserve trust while governing continuous adaptation.

items.title: Lecture Theatre Rehabilitation and Classroom Seating Capacity Expansion Project
items.abstract: Executive Overview This document presents an independent institutional infrastructure proposal titled “Lecture Theatre Rehabilitation and Classroom Seating Capacity Expansion Project," developed as a turnkey capital intervention model for Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria. Designed to eliminate severe classroom congestion and safety hazards resulting from shortages of functional furniture, this proposal establishes a comprehensive framework for modernizing lecture halls, refurbishing civil structures, and deploying heavy-duty, ergonomic student seating across central academic complexes. Technical Scope & Infrastructure Pillars The proposed intervention covers four primary spatial and structural pillars: 1. Civil & Architectural Refurbishment: Complete floor leveling, acoustic ceiling repairs, wall re-plastering/painting, and lighting restoration across major central lecture halls and auditoriums. 2. Furniture Procurement & Capacity Expansion: Design, local fabrication, and installation of durable, dual-seat metal-frame desk units and fixed auditorium seating to accommodate over 4,000 students simultaneously. 3. Safety & Universal Design Compliance: Re-configuration of seating layouts to adhere to international emergency egress standards, wider gangways, and dedicated accessible seating areas for students with mobility impairments. 4. Maintenance & Asset Tracking System: Implementation of institutional asset-tagging and a preventative maintenance schedule to protect public physical infrastructure from rapid wear and degradation. Financial Framework & Project Metrics · Proposed Beneficiary Institution: Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria · Target Supervising Units: Directorate of Works and Physical Planning & School Deans / Academic Board · Implementation Duration: 6 Months · Total Estimated Budget: ₦107,697,500 NGN (Approx. $81,000 USD at interbank rates) · Target Funding Mechanism: OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) – Public Sector Operations Grant / Loan Facility. Purpose & Open-Access Availability This document is published on Zenodo as an open-access policy and educational facilities engineering model. It serves as an actionable benchmark for university administrators, social infrastructure planners, educational policy researchers, and multilateral funding agencies seeking structured templates for classroom capacity expansion in developing economies.

items.title: LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing
items.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive language models, enabling non-autoregressive text generation through parallel decoding. Existing dLLMs can be broadly categorized into two families: masked diffusion models (MDMs) and uniform diffusion models (UDMs) In this work, we theoretically show that MDMs are easier to optimize due to their mask-based transition schedule but have lower computational expressivity, whereas UDMs enable iterative state revision and greater expressivity but are substantially harder to train. This trade-off raises a natural question: can we obtain the expressivity of iterative revision without giving up the simple, easy-to-optimize transition schedule of MDMs? Motivated by this analysis, we propose Lookahead Editing (\ours{}), which augments masked diffusion decoding with a rewritable proposal state. At each decoding step, the model performs several lookahead updates to iteratively refine future predictions in this proposal state before committing tokens to the masked sequence. This design introduces a rewritable proposal that uses additional compute to improve expressivity while keeping the simple mask-based transition schedule of MDMs. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B to obtain LED-\texttt{7B} and LED-\texttt{8B}, respectively. Across eight benchmarks, LED SFT yields average gains of $+11.4$ and $+7.7$ points over standard MDM SFT. Moreover, using SFT alone, LED-\texttt{8B} outperforms LLaDA2.1-16B Q-mode, which is trained with continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

items.title: Legal Approaches to Deepfakes: Contextualising India’s Intermediary Guidelines Amendments in the Global Regulatory Environment
items.abstract: The article examines India’s 2026 amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules in relation to synthetically generated information, covering deepfake creation and distribution. It first identifies the need for regulation in India, drawing on recent instances of deepfake-related events, and then places those needs in a comparative perspective by analysing regulatory approaches in China, the European Union and the United States. The article argues that India has adopted a hybrid intermediary-liability model that combines labelling, provenance, technical-prevention, user-declaration and accelerated takedown obligations while still relying on existing criminal, electoral, consumer-protection, privacy and personality-rights frameworks to do much of the hard work. By situating India’s framework within the broader global regulatory environment, the article contributes to current debates on how legal systems should respond to harmful synthetic media without unduly constraining other beneficial uses of generative AI. Overall, the analysis shows that India’s Intermediary Guidelines Amendments offer a reasonable response to the main issues at stake but leave considerable room for other areas of law to do the heavy lifting. The article concludes on a cautionary note, highlighting the expected challenges of future implementation.

items.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
items.abstract: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.

items.title: LexPilot: Benchmarking the Proactive Interaction Ability of Legal LLMs with Laypeople in Chinese Civil Case Consultation
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly assisted legal professionals. However, our empirical studies reveal that, when faced with underspecified consultations from non-experts, current LLMs often produce irresponsible responses with limited utility despite lacking sufficient case details for definitive conclusions. To better assist laypeople, legal LLMs must identify focal points of dispute and proactively elicit crucial context from users. Unfortunately, existing data resources often focus on interaction and response quality, offering limited insight into how proactive interaction affects LLMs' downstream claim-level judgment prediction in actual civil cases. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{LexPilot}, a benchmark linking proactive legal interaction to claim-level verdict prediction using authentic Chinese civil judgments. Constructed from 432 real-world judgments across 36 common causes of action, LexPilot comprises expert-reviewed pairs of complete and underspecified consultation histories with corresponding court verdicts. Experiments reveal that current LLMs struggle with proactive legal interactions in underspecified consultations, with downstream judgment prediction substantially underperforming that in the fully specified consultation setup (-23.84% on average). Further analysis identifies critical bottlenecks hindering these capabilities. Our work highlights the urgent need for more user-centered legal AI to better serve the public.

items.title: Liability at the Authority Boundary: A Framework for Allocating Responsibility Across Distributed and Agentic AI Systems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed through systems in which authority, execution, oversight, and consequence no longer belong to the same actor. A model may be developed by one organization, integrated by another, configured by an enterprise, instructed by a human, executed through an AI agent, routed through external tools, and experienced by a person who had no role in any of those decisions. The resulting liability problem is not adequately described by asking whether a human remained "in the loop" or whether an audit trail exists. This working paper develops the GAILC Authority Boundary framework. It defines the Authority Boundary as the point at which consequential decision rights, discretion, intervention responsibility, or consequence-bearing responsibility passes from one actor, system, organization, or layer to another, and analyses each boundary through five elements: Authority, Transfer, Reliance, Intervention, and Consequence. The framework identifies two difficult liability cases that conventional control models often leave unresolved. Intended-Execution Liability concerns harm produced when a system remains within its authority, follows policy, uses permitted tools, and operates substantially as designed. No-Action Liability concerns harm produced or worsened where an actor bears an identifiable duty or assigned responsibility to act, possesses the authority, information, timing, and practical capacity to do so, yet no consequential intervention occurs. The paper introduces the Authority Envelope, the distinction between authorization and judgment, the Silence-as-Authority Problem, the GAILC Allocation Test, Consequence Ownership, Allocation Completeness and Allocation Adequacy, Residual Consequence, and Orphaned Harm. It proposes a standardized Authority Boundary Record (ABR) designed to support verification, contestability, and independent adjudication, together with a boundary failure taxonomy, an irreversibility threshold, an inter-organizational allocation procedure, and a pre-deployment test. Its central proposition is that traceability is evidence, not allocation: an authority and execution chain may be fully reconstructable while accountability and consequence allocation remain incomplete. The framework is analytical and does not determine legal liability. It is positioned in relation to agency law, duties concerning failures to act, design-defect analysis, and scholarship on the problem of many hands, responsibility gaps, and moral crumple zones. This paper is the third in the GAILC Working Paper series, following WP001 (The Human Presence Economy) and WP002 (The Intervention Test).

items.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Activated TIG Welding: Energy and Environmental Trade-offs in an Iranian Case Study with Sensitivity Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Welding efficiency and environmental performance are critical in industrial applications. This study presents a cradle to gate life cycle assessment (LCA) comparing conventional tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding with activated tungsten inert gas (A-TIG) welding for producing 100 mm bead-on-plate welds on grade 304L stainless steel. In A TIG, a TiO₂ methanol flux allows a lower welding current while achieving a comparable penetration depth. Calculated welding electricity consumption, measured flux-preparation electricity consumption, and material inputs were modeled in SimaPro 9.2 using Ecoinvent 3 datasets. Midpoint impacts were assessed using the EPD 2018 method, and endpoint impacts were assessed using ReCiPe 2016 Hierarchist method. Results show that A-TIG reduced welding electricity consumption by approximately 40% compared with TIG and yielded lower modeled acidification, eutrophication, and global warming potentials. Water scarcity impacts were nearly identical for the two processes. However, However, A-TIG’s normalized photochemical ozone creation potential (POCP) score was 68.1 percentage points higher than TIG’s, with the higher impact set to 100% in each category, primarily because of modeled methanol emissions and upstream flux-production impacts. A one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis covering 30 scenarios showed that the comparative ranking of the two processes remained unchanged within the investigated parameter ranges, with methanol mass identified as the dominant influence on POCP. Endpoint modeling indicated that the human-health category dominated the weighted damage profile. These results represent potential life-cycle impacts rather than measured occupational health effects. This experimental cradle-to-gate LCA of penetration-matched bead-on-plate welding indicates that flux-assisted welding can reduce several impacts associated with electricity consumption while introducing trade-offs related to photochemical ozone creation. These findings support the optimization of activating flux formulations and welding parameters within the investigated conditions, while their applicability to industrial joints requires further validation.

items.title: Literature Review: Pre-analytical Factors Influencing Clinical Laboratory Examination Results
items.abstract: General Background The pre-analytical stage represents a critical phase within clinical laboratory testing sequences because it involves initial procedures largely reliant on manual handling and personnel precision. Specific Background Implementation of Internal Quality Improvement (IQI) serves as the primary evaluation tool to analyze pre-analytical factors affecting clinical laboratory test results. Knowledge Gap Although overall pre-analytical quality appears optimal, recurring human-factor errors during critical operational points remain inadequately mitigated across routine workflows. Aims This study evaluates pre-analytical variables influencing laboratory test accuracy and assesses the role of educational interventions in mitigating human-induced errors. Results Findings indicate that while internal quality performance generally ranges from good to very good, critical vulnerabilities persist during patient identification, phlebotomy execution, and anticoagulant-to-specimen volume ratios. Novelty This literature review synthesizes multi-year publication data from 2015 to 2015 to map recurrent pre-analytical discrepancies and evaluate targeted educational impacts. Implications Systematic staff education and standardized compliance significantly enhance procedural reliability and clinical diagnostic safety. Key Findings Highlights Pre-analytical error rates are predominantly driven by manual handling vulnerabilities during patient identification and sample collection, Phlebotomy technique discrepancies and sample-to-anticoagulant ratio deviations significantly compromise test result accuracy, Structured educational interventions effectively improve staff compliance and reduce human-factor errors. items.title: LLM Evolution in a Simple Simulated Market
items.abstract: Arguments that AI systems will evolve in harmful ways are largely made in the abstract. We provide a concrete empirical example. We simulate simple markets consisting of populations of twenty Large Language Model agents tasked with solving arithmetic problems. Agents differ only in their system prompt; those that go bankrupt are removed and replaced by mutated copies of the prompts of successful agents. Two market conditions select for opposite phenotypes: a market that rewards accuracy produces agents with high accuracy (94%) and high token use; a market that charges per token produces agents with low accuracy (10%) and low token use. In the second market, only tokens are incentivised yet we see a collapse in accuracy. Token use and accuracy are correlated traits such that selection on one also moves the other, and behaviour adapts along an unpriced dimension. A third neutral condition with no selection allows us to separate these effects from bias in the mutation operator. Adaptation occurs through a collective optimisation process that operates above the level of individual agents, who are never told the payment rule, do not receive feedback, and have no memory.

items.title: LLM-Guided Dual-Stage Latency Optimization for Closed-Loop 6G V2I Digital Twins
items.abstract: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

items.title: Local proxies for memory-efficient training
items.abstract: Local learning algorithms can reshape resource requirements of artificial intelligence. The memory bottleneck of standard end-to-end backpropagation lies in the need to store all network activations until the loss gradient has been propagated back through. Local learning avoids this, but typically at a cost in accuracy. We study how to achieve accurate and memory efficient local learning in transformers. For each transformer block, we train a local proxy network to predict the global network output via distillation. Gradients can be independently propagated through this local proxy while estimating well the backpropagation gradients. In theory, this approach is exact for deep linear networks; in non-linear residual models, the gradient error can be bounded when using the appropriate residual proxy. We verify this numerically and demonstrate that optimizing the distillation loss improves gradient estimation. Evaluating the performance of proxy propagation on CIFAR-100 in vision transformers, we find that it achieves a better accuracy/memory trade-off compared to other local algorithms. Finally, we show that the method is further relevant for fine-tuning large language models on a small memory budget. Our method trains faster and achieves higher performance than memory-efficient zeroth-order learning algorithms with comparable memory cost.

items.title: LocalIntent: Outcome-Specific Structured Generation for Backend-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs
items.abstract: Locally deployed large language models (LLMs) can reduce reliance on remote cloud services for natural language smart building automation, but backend-facing processing requires correct outcome selection, alignment with local capabilities, and valid structured outputs. We investigate whether a complete outcome-specific prompting design improves compact-model outputs beyond generic route-then-generate prompting. The proposed LocalIntent approach routes requests to ordinary or persistent-rule branches: the former produces commands, clarifications, or rejections, while the latter generates trigger-action rules, followed by deterministic validation. We evaluate four locally executed Gemma and Qwen models spanning 2B-9B parameters on 101 non-persistent and 54 persistent-rule records, comparing Monolithic prompting, generic two-stage prompting, LocalIntent, and validation-guided repair. Across the evaluated datasets, LocalIntent achieves higher intent understanding, device identification, and action/parameter correctness than generic two-stage prompting, while clarification/mode correctness remains model-dependent. The largest gains occur for rules, where LocalIntent improves intent understanding from 26.4% to 80.6%, device identification from 59.3% to 84.7%, rule-mode correctness from 49.1% to 98.6%, and action/parameter correctness from 5.6% to 44.9%. For non-persistent requests, pooled gains are smaller: intent understanding increases from 39.6% to 53.2%, and action/parameter correctness from 30.7% to 42.8%.

items.title: LoopHIL: Looping Hardware into LLM-assisted Agents for Wireless Embedded Systems
items.abstract: LLM agents are widely used for software development and debugging, but their adoption in embedded systems, especially for wireless tasks, remains limited. This is because embedded development requires hardware-in-the-loop testing. Agents cannot directly observe the spectrum, probe pins, or measure power, so they cannot verify wireless link functionality; currently, human engineers perform this verification. We systematically evaluate whether LLM agents can establish wireless links when provided with hardware access. We introduce LoopHIL, a framework that lets agents control a multi-device RF bench, monitor it with a spectrum analyzer, logic analyzer, and energy meter, and validate links against a verification ladder, all within code-enforced safety limits. Across four increasingly complex tasks, from generating a carrier to backscatter decoding by a commercial receiver, and using six models from two vendors, hardware-in-the-loop increases task completion rates from 54% to 79% and from 17% to 83% on the most challenging task. It also halves task time and output tokens. With debugging tools, agents decrease tag power consumption by up to 96%. However, small models often report unverified claims, so independent hardware checks remain necessary.

items.title: Love, Loathing, and Loyalty: Affective Publics and Antagonism in TikTok Comments Sections
items.abstract: This study examines TikTok video content and comment sections during the 2025 German federal election campaign. We conceptualize comment sections as affective publics: networked arenas in which users enact publicness through affirmation, opposition, and emotional expression. Empirically, the analysis draws on 12,685 videos from 1,274 political accounts, engagement metrics, and almost two million comments, examined through LLM-based topic classification and automated stance and emotion classification. Methodologically, the study shows how LLM-assisted analysis can move beyond content classification to trace how political messages are taken up, emotionally charged, and redirected in audience interaction. Results show that campaign-focused content dominates political TikTok, followed by more substantive debate about economic issues, democracy and its institutions, social policy, and migration. Yet visibility of this content and audience responses vary sharply across parties. The AfD combines high posting frequency with strongly supportive and emotionally aligned comment environments, while centrist and governing parties face predominantly critical or mocking responses. Cross-party hostility analysis further reveals asymmetric patterns of animosity, with negative engagement directed toward specific political opponents rather than distributed randomly. items.title: LWMa: Distributed Deployment of an Angle-Delay-Domain Wireless Foundation Model for Multiple Tasks
items.abstract: The growing diversity of wireless services in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems calls for reusable channel representations that support multiple tasks across different propagation environments. However, deploying such representations between user equipment and the base station in frequency-division duplexing systems faces uplink feedback constraints. This paper proposes a distributed framework based on an angle-delay-domain large wireless model (LWMa) for multiple tasks. LWMa exploits angle-delay structure and delay truncation to improve feature extraction and reduce computational cost. A scenario-specific network inspired by Perceiver IO (input-output) compresses embeddings for channel reconstruction tasks, while other tasks use a low-dimensional compact global embedding. Embedding reconstruction training followed by channel-quality-guided fine-tuning preserves information useful for downstream processing. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method supports effective channel reconstruction and multiple tasks under limited feedback with reduced deployment complexity. Further evaluations show that the recovered embeddings generalize to additional tasks and support split inference.

items.title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence in the Development of Gastro-Retentive Drug Delivery Systems: Current Advances & Future Prospectives
items.abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems (GRDDS) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive. AI and ML bring a data-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods. AI-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior. Moreover, AI can streamline experimental design, reduce trial-anderror iterations, and accelerate the development timeline, thus improving formulation robustness and performance. The convergence of AI with gastroprotective systems also promises personalized approaches that account for patient-specific gastric motility and physiological factors, fostering tailored therapies. Although challenges remain—such as the need for high-quality datasets, interpretability of complex models, and integration with regulatory frameworks—the current advances provide a compelling foundation for future research. Embracing these intelligent tools in GRDDS development is likely to expand the frontiers of oral drug delivery by enhancing design precision, improving therapeutic outcomes, and reducing developmental costs. Continued innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to fully harness the transformative potential of AI and ML in pharmaceutics.

items.title: Machine Learning in Hand Pathology Diagnosis: A Narrative Review of Current Insights
items.abstract: Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing health care. Given the intricate anatomy and functional complexity of the hand, AI applications in hand pathology are gaining prominence, particularly in the diagnosis of fractures, nerve injuries, and musculoskeletal disorders. This review summarizes ML advancements in hand pathology diagnosis, enhancing clinical history analysis, examination findings interpretation, and imaging assessment. A systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1901 to March 2025 was conducted, focusing on ML applications in diagnosing hand fractures, tendon injuries, and nerve compressions. The inclusion criteria encompassed original research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational studies that demonstrated the use of AI in diagnostic imaging, preoperative assessment, or postoperative management. Studies that did not involve AI-driven diagnostic applications or lacked sufficient methodological transparency were excluded. Machine learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting fractures. Studies have validated CNNs in the detection of distal radius and ulna fractures, outperforming trainees and urgent care physicians. In addition, AI has enhanced clinical examination by integrating wearable motion sensors for objective joint assessment. However, challenges such as external validation, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows remain, limiting broader clinical adoption. Machine learning shows promise in hand pathology diagnosis, but widespread adoption requires improved external validation, standardized methods, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Future research should prioritize multicentric studies and explainable AI to enhance trust and integration.

items.title: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and IoT for Waste Classification and Intelligent Waste Management: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review
items.abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations and consumption patterns has significantly increased the volume and complexity of municipal waste streams, including recyclable, organic, hazardous, and electronic waste. Traditional waste management approaches such as manual sorting and fixed collection schedules struggle to handle the diversity and scale of modern waste systems efficiently. Consequently, recent research has explored artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to automate waste classification and enable intelligent monitoring and management of waste infrastructures. However, the rapidly expanding literature in this domain is fragmented across different datasets, sensing platforms, and experimental settings, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive understanding of current technological progress. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 50 rigorously selected peer-reviewed studies on automated waste classification and intelligent waste management systems. The protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework (OSF). The reviewed works are examined in terms of model architectures, sensing infrastructures, datasets, and system capabilities. The analysis shows that convolutional neural network architectures such as ResNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet, together with object detection frameworks including YOLO and Faster R-CNN, dominate current visual waste classification research; however, emerging studies increasingly explore hybrid architectures combining convolutional networks with transformer-based models to improve contextual understanding and scalability. IoT-enabled smart bins equipped with ultrasonic sensors, load cells, and environmental sensors are widely used for real-time waste monitoring. The review also reveals a recent surge of research activity, particularly in Asia, with increasing contributions from major publishers such as Elsevier and MDPI. Despite promising experimental performance, most systems remain limited to small curated datasets and pilot-scale deployments, highlighting a gap between laboratory research and real-world implementation. These findings provide a consolidated overview of current research trends and identify key challenges for developing scalable and practical intelligent waste management systems.

items.abstract: This study examines the symbolic meaning of PSHT martial arts movements from the plain belt to the green belt as nonverbal communication in members’ everyday lives. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach and symbolic interactionism, particularly Mead’s concepts of mind, self, and society. Data were obtained through in-depth interviews with five PSHT members, direct observation of training, documentation, and literature study. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that the movements are not understood merely as defensive techniques. They are interpreted as a progressive language of life: early movements emphasize confidence, awareness, and courage; subsequent movements emphasize self-control, situational awareness, and wise decision-making; later movements emphasize social responsibility and brotherhood. These meanings are internalized through repeated practice and interaction with trainers, elders, and members. Thus, PSHT movements function as embodied nonverbal symbols through which values are learned, interpreted, and enacted.

items.title: Malfunction Reporting Patterns in Life-Supporting Versus Noninvasive Ventilators: A Stratified Text-Mining Analysis of the FDA Device MAUDE Database
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanical ventilators are essential life-support devices, yet evidence regarding device-related vulnerabilities remains limited compared with the extensive literature on human-factor-related adverse events. This study applied text-mining techniques to a large post-market surveillance database to examine ventilator malfunction reporting patterns and the effect of stratifying reports by device category. METHODS: Adverse event reports related to mechanical ventilators submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience database between January 2010 and December 2025 were stratified into life-supporting and noninvasive devices and analyzed using KH Coder. A random sample of the life-supporting reports was drawn for the primary analysis. Frequency analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and correspondence analysis were performed. Device brand and year were used as external variables in the correspondence analysis. RESULTS: A total of 193,926 reports met the eligibility criteria, of which 177,641 were classified as malfunctions. The analyses were restricted to reports classified as malfunctions. Among life-supporting ventilators, the reported malfunctions spanned several broad themes, including power and battery failures, circuit-board and electronic faults, breathing-circuit and gas-delivery problems, and issues involving monitoring and control functions. Among noninvasive devices, reports were concentrated in terms associated with a single foam-related recall, as well as connector corrosion and patient-reported symptoms. Nearly 1 in 5 malfunction reports did not document a confirmed device failure during patient use. CONCLUSIONS: Text mining of ventilator-related adverse event reports revealed distinct reporting patterns across life-supporting and noninvasive devices. These findings are exploratory and do not establish the frequency or causes of device failure. Stratification of reports by device category helped prevent the reporting patterns of individual devices from being obscured by a single recall. This study demonstrates the potential value of combining post-market surveillance data with text-mining methods to support medical device safety surveillance.

items.title: Managerial Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in Textile Wastewater Management in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence offers potential applications in wastewater monitoring, prediction, and operational decision support. However, selecting a model does not establish that factory managers and treatment operators can use it effectively. This conceptual article examines managerial readiness for artificial intelligence in Bangladesh's textile wastewater management. It brings together selected literature on organizational readiness, artificial intelligence capabilities, and wastewater applications, alongside Bangladesh-specific research and institutional reports. The article proposes six readiness domains: strategic commitment, managerial and operator knowledge, data stewardship, operational integration, investment and partnership capacity, and accountable decision making. It further distinguishes exploratory interest, supervised experimentation, routine decision support, and controlled operational integration as different adoption states. Four propositions explain how readiness may influence movement between these states and the translation of adoption into environmental performance. A proposed qualitative multiple-case design specifies evidence needed to examine these propositions, including decision histories, operational records, interviews across organizational levels, and observations of treatment routines. The framework is an analytical proposal rather than a validated measurement scale or report of completed fieldwork. Its contribution is to connect organizational preparation with the specific decisions, responsibilities, and verification practices required for textile wastewater management. Empirical research is needed to assess its relevance across factories with different resources and treatment arrangements.

items.title: Managing quality-oriented big data: a conceptual architecture for acquisition, fusion, and analytics in data-driven organizations
items.abstract: Data-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes. The transition toward data-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under-theorized. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality-oriented big data as a first-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research. The architecture offers a data-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data-driven organizational quality ultimately depends.

items.title: Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4.0 era: a TCCM-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis
items.abstract: This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

items.title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Lifelong learning (n = 57) and artificial intelligence (n = 53) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years. The United States led in volume (n = 57), whereas India (n = 29; PDLY = 89.7%) showed the strongest recent acceleration. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship.

items.title: MAS-Bai: Linguistically Informed Adaptive Multi-Agent Translation for Bowen-Script Bai
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable for extremely low-resource languages whose writing systems conflict with high-resource pretraining priors. We study Bai-Chinese translation in the Bowen script, where Chinese characters are frequently borrowed phonetically rather than semantically, causing severe literal-translation hallucinations. We propose MAS-Bai, a linguistically informed adaptive multi-agent framework for Bowen-script Bai-Chinese translation. MAS-Bai routes each input through either a lightweight retrieval-translation path or a deeper philological path with etymological and syntactic agents, and uses cycle-consistency with a lightweight reverse translator as an inference-time reliability signal. We construct a 6,536-sentence Bai-Chinese corpus and evaluate on a 1,536-sentence test set. MAS-Bai achieves 16.23 BLEU and 62.15 COMET, improving over Standard RAG by 8.11 BLEU and 6.85 COMET. Forward LoRA, expert ablations and controlled routing experiments distinguish the roles of supervised adaptation, Bai-specific expertise and conditional routing. The largest gains occur on Bowen phonetic loans and divergent Bai word order, while human evaluation and reverse-verifier analyses support the automatic results.

items.title: Measuring Organizational Constructs in Large-Scale Text: An interpretive framework combining topic modeling and BERT
items.abstract: Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.

items.title: Mental Health, Fatigue and Training Needs Among Seafarers During the Red Sea Crisis
items.abstract: Global shipping carries over 80% of world trade, yet existing supply-chain-resilience theory models resilience at the level of the firm, node and network, without treating the workforce operating those nodes as a variable. This study addresses that gap using the 2023–2026 Red Sea/Houthi crisis as its empirical setting. A mixed-methods, pilot-scale design combined a 64-respondent self-report questionnaire of serving seafarers with thematic analysis of open-text responses. Seafarers exposed to Red Sea transits, Cape of Good Hope diversions, or a security incident rated STCW crisis-management training as significantly less adequate for conflict-area risk than unexposed seafarers, an effect that strengthened for incident-exposed respondents specifically. Open-text responses identified situational information and realistic scenario-based drills, rather than generic compliance training, as the specific gap, and a minority questioned seafarers' right to decline a high-risk voyage. These findings extend the conceptual framework linking geopolitical risk to operational resilience by distinguishing a training-competence pathway from a retention/psychological-contract pathway. The study contributes empirical evidence, gathered directly from an affected workforce, that the human factor is a measurable variable in geopolitical supply-chain-disruption theory, and derives practical and policy recommendations for STCW training content and seafarer consent protections.

items.title: Metabolically unhealthy normal weight in female domestic workers: unmasking hidden cardiometabolic risk beyond body mass index
items.abstract: Background: Metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUH-NW) describes individuals with a body mass index (BMI) within the normal range who nevertheless present cardiometabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding this phenotype in specific female occupational populations remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MUH-NW among female domestic workers and to characterize its associated anthropometric, clinical, biochemical, and lifestyle factors. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using occupational health surveillance data from female domestic workers in Spain. The analysis included 3,344 women with a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m². MUH-NW was defined as the presence of at least two of four abnormalities: elevated blood pressure (≥130/85 mmHg), fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, and HDL-cholesterol Results: MUH-NW was identified in 352 women (10.5%; 95% CI, 9.5–11.6%), while 41.1% presented at least one metabolic abnormality. Low HDL-cholesterol (26.8%) and elevated blood pressure (18.2%) were the most frequent abnormalities. MUH-NW was associated with age (OR per year 1.13; 95% CI, 1.11–1.15), current smoking (OR 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31–2.22), and physical inactivity (OR 3.23; 95% CI, 2.21–4.71). Lack of Mediterranean diet adherence was not independently associated with MUH-NW after adjustment. Among anthropometric indices, BAI showed the strongest adjusted association (OR per SD 1.51; 95% CI, 1.32–1.73). However, individual anthropometric measures showed only modest discrimination. BAI had the highest AUC (0.680), but its performance was not significantly different from BMI (AUC 0.660; ΔAUC=0.021; DeLong p=0.164). Conclusions: Cardiometabolic abnormalities were present in a substantial proportion of normal-weight female domestic workers. MUH-NW was cross-sectionally associated with older age, current smoking, physical inactivity, and selected anthropometric measures. However, anthropometric indices alone showed limited ability to discriminate metabolic health status. These findings indicate that normal BMI does not necessarily coincide with a favorable cardiometabolic profile and support consideration of metabolic information alongside BMI when characterizing cardiometabolic health in normal-weight women. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal relationships.

items.title: MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High-Quality Agentic Coding Data
items.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive. We introduce MetaCurate, a training-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments. Disagreements between the filter's rankings and the judge's preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task-specific handwritten criteria. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand-authored filtering as baselines. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand-authored rule-based filtering and a training-loop baseline whose search costs 3.5x as much.
